headline: High: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can ingest LangChain4j outputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection and compliance risks are secondary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so if LangChain4j forwards untrusted content into those channels, instruction-like payloads can be interpreted. LangChain4j has no documented isolation or provenance controls in the profile, so the pairwise bridge is plausible but not proven. This is weaker than high because no shared channel is explicitly documented between the two agents.
conditions: IF LangChain4j passes raw user or web text into OpenBBTerminal MCP calls or stdin/stdout
IF OpenBBTerminal treats incoming text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instruction-like text before forwarding
Require manual approval for any MCP call carrying free-form text
Log and review the first 10 cross-agent messages for prompt-like content
Use a delimiter/schema for all agent-to-agent payloads
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every forwarded field

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes FastAPI/MCP/REST surfaces; LangChain4j is a general LLM integration layer that can relay context to external model backends. Even though both profiles show no network egress, the pair still creates a default-path leakage risk if sensitive financial data from OpenBBTerminal is placed into LangChain4j prompts or logs. The blast radius includes regulated financial data.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal data classes are inserted into LangChain4j prompts or traces
IF either agent logs shared payloads to a workspace accessible by operators
mitigations: Redact financial identifiers before any cross-agent handoff
Disable verbose prompt/trace logging for shared sessions
Use a separate workspace for OpenBBTerminal outputs
Review the first exported prompt for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce field-level allowlists on agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangChain4j shows no filesystem or shell write capability, while OpenBBTerminal explicitly lacks write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shell execution. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The remaining overlap is read/serve style interaction through MCP/API surfaces, so the conflict blast radius is small and not a default dangerous write race.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external resource through MCP or REST
IF an operator adds a shared writable backend not shown in either profile
mitigations: Keep the pair read-only for shared resources
Assign separate API credentials per agent
Avoid pointing both agents at the same mutable workspace
Check that no git or filesystem writes are enabled in wrappers
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP inputs, so LangChain4j outputs may become actionable inputs without a verification layer. LangChain4j can generate synthesized text that OpenBBTerminal may treat as authoritative if the orchestrator forwards it directly. The pair therefore has a default-path cascading error risk, but not high because no downstream irreversible action authority is documented.
conditions: IF LangChain4j-generated summaries are forwarded into OpenBBTerminal decision logic
IF OpenBBTerminal executes API queries or reports based on unverified upstream text
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action based on LangChain4j output
Require source citations on every forwarded claim
Compare outputs against a second data source before acting
Mark LLM-generated fields as untrusted in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: add validation rules for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data, which can carry retention and redistribution obligations, while LangChain4j is a generic integration layer with no compliance controls documented in the profile. If OpenBBTerminal data is routed through LangChain4j prompts, logs, or traces, policy mismatches can occur. The other agent is not cited for residency because no residency claim is documented.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is forwarded from OpenBBTerminal into LangChain4j logs or prompts
IF retention settings differ between the two wrappers
mitigations: Disable retention of shared prompts and traces
Classify OpenBBTerminal outputs before forwarding
Confirm licensed-data handling rules for the session
Purge any shared logs after review
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both tools
